thread.title_full: Tulsa City Council extends downtown teen curfew for one year - NewsBreak

author: MaKayla Glenn
title: Tulsa City Council extends downtown teen curfew for one year - NewsBreak
text:
By MaKayla Glenn ,
8 hours ago
The Tulsa City Council voted unanimously Wednesday night to extend the downtown teen curfew for another year.
The ordinance, first approved this summer after several high-profile crimes involving teenagers, was set to expire this week.
The council’s vote keeps the restrictions in place as some Tulsans question whether the policy sends the wrong message to young people.
What does the downtown Tulsa curfew include? The curfew now applies from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays for anyone 17 or younger in the downtown Tulsa area.
Councilors removed Thursdays from the curfew after city data showed few issues on that night.
Why did the City Council extend the curfew? Tulsa City Councilor Lori Decter Wright said the extension is about safety and crowd control following incidents that happened earlier this year.
“It’s really about crowd control and some of the things that we really saw flare up this summer,” Decter Wright said.
She added that the council reviewed community feedback and data before deciding to reduce the curfew to two nights.
“It was actually some of the people that made the initial request who said that Thursday is not actually reflected in the data that we needed,” Decter Wright said.
Decter-Wright said five teenagers have been cited for violating the curfew since June, most in the first few months after it took effect.
What do critics of the downtown Tulsa curfew say? Not everyone agrees the curfew should remain in place.
Tulsa resident Evan Taylor said he believes the curfew unfairly punishes teens who aren’t causing problems.
“I just wanted to get my voice in for the people that are not here — the youth who don’t know to show up to city council, because they’re busy dealing with after-school programs or playing football or studying,” Taylor said.
Taylor said he hopes city leaders will consider giving teens their “privileges” back sooner rather than later.
“In this year, I would love to see you guys come with the carrot and be like, we’re giving it back to you, but just know we can take it away,” Taylor said.
What do supporters of the curfew say? Tulsa City Councilor Laura Bellis said the policy is not meant to keep teenagers away but to keep everyone safe.
“This isn’t a ‘You can’t be here.’ It’s just trying to encourage a safe way to be present,” Bellis said. “I would view it as a harm reduction tool while simultaneously, we know we need to provide other safe third spaces for youth to hang out.”
Bellis said finding safer, fun spaces for young people to gather remains an important priority for the city.
What happens next? City leaders said they will review curfew data quarterly, including reports from the Tulsa Police Department, before deciding next October whether to lift or modify the curfew.
MaKayla Glenn MaKayla Glenn is an Emmy-nominated journalist. She started with News On 6 in August 2022.
